rows.grounds: negation + inferior/secondary + primary-connection; denies attribution through a lesser primary basis
one who partakes of grossness or materiality

items.question: Can Shiva ever partake of grossness through association with an inferior principle?
premises: Shiva is the supreme reality
Grossness belongs to inferior manifestation
Association with inferiority does not define Shiva
items.inference: Shiva never becomes gross through connection with an inferior principle.
items.plain_english: Shiva never becomes gross, not even through association with an inferior principle.

rows.grounds: in the explanatory gloss or commentary

items.question: What is the status of the apparent identity of Shiva with grossness?
premises: Manifestation of identity with that appears
Such appearance is error
The commentary has explained this fully
items.inference: The apparent identity of Shiva with grossness is only an error, as explained in the commentary.
items.plain_english: The manifestation of identity with that is an error; thus everything has been explained in the commentary.

items.question: Does the designation of a thing as milk exist at the very instant of transformation?
premises: A designation depends on recognizable form
Transformation alters the prior state
At that instant the prior designation fails
items.inference: The designation 'this is milk' does not exist at that very moment.
items.plain_english: And the designation 'this is milk' does not exist at that very moment.

rows.grounds: refers to the preceding state or process
relative reference to the prior phase

items.question: Why must prior and later phases be distinguished in the process of manifestation?
premises: A process involves successive phases
Designation depends on a specific phase
The earlier phase must be identified separately
items.inference: Prior and later parts must be conceived to understand the change.
items.plain_english: Its prior and later parts must be conceived, for there is indeed the earlier phase.

rows.grounds: unfolding of the ground of consciousness

items.question: What characterizes the initial phase of manifestation in consciousness?
premises: Manifestation begins in consciousness
The first phase is an expansion
This has been stated earlier
items.inference: The initial phase is the expansion of the abode of consciousness.
items.plain_english: It is said to be the expansion of the abode of consciousness.

rows.grounds: capacity for knowing and seeing its own activity

items.question: What capacity arises immediately after the expansion of consciousness?
premises: Expansion is followed by a further phase
Consciousness manifests its own activity
Knowing and seeing powers emerge
items.inference: Immediately after comes the power of knowing and seeing its own activity.
items.plain_english: Immediately after, indeed, comes the power of knowing and seeing its own activity.

rows.grounds: refers to the power just described

items.question: How does the arising of action-power relate to the establishment of the world?
premises: The described power is action-power
Action-power arises in sequence
The world depends on this arising
items.inference: From the arising of action-power the entire world becomes established.
items.plain_english: That is declared to be the power of action; thence the entire world is established.

rows.grounds: because practical effects are obtained, as stated

items.question: Why is the world said to be established through practical effects?
premises: Practical effects become attainable
Attainment of effects grounds experience
This explains worldly establishment
items.inference: Because practical effects are attained, the whole world is said to be established.
items.plain_english: It is said that because practical effects are attained, thence the entire world is established.

rows.grounds: nor is orientation ceased; sandhi na+ca+aunmukhyaṃ

items.question: Do orientation and cessation ever fully disappear in the dynamic of consciousness?
premises: Consciousness remains dynamic
Orientation toward manifestation persists
Complete cessation is not absolute
items.inference: Neither withdrawal, nor orientation, nor cessation is absolutely ended.
items.plain_english: It has not ceased, nor has orientation ceased, nor even is there cessation.

rows.grounds: in relation to the fivefold power

items.question: What is meant by the term cessation in the context of the fivefold power?
premises: The term cessation is used
It refers to a power of consciousness
It must be understood within the fivefold scheme
items.inference: By the word cessation, the full power of consciousness is understood in relation to the fivefold power.
items.plain_english: Or by the word 'cessation' the full power of consciousness is understood in relation to the fivefold power.

items.question: What follows for all things from the full power of consciousness?
premises: Consciousness underlies all phases
All things arise within its power
Their essence is therefore unified
items.inference: Therefore all things are established in a single harmony of essence.
items.plain_english: Therefore, the harmony of all things is established.

rows.grounds: with respect to the duality of orientation and cessation

items.question: From what dual perspective are the states of consciousness being considered?
premises: Consciousness can be described in phases
Orientation and cessation form a pair
Analysis depends on this duality
items.inference: The discussion proceeds with regard to the duality of orientation and cessation.
items.plain_english: With regard to the duality of orientation and cessation.

rows.grounds: absence of experience without desire or will

items.question: Can knowledge or experience occur without the presence of consciousness?
premises: Knowing is an act of consciousness
Experience requires conscious presence
Without consciousness experience is absent
items.inference: Knowledge occurs only here in consciousness; without it there is no desireless experience.
uncertainties: The compound niricchorvedanakṣatiḥ admits more than one syntactic reading.
items.plain_english: Knowledge knows only here; without consciousness there is no experience.

items.question: Can aversion or cognition operate independently of consciousness?
premises: Aversion is directed activity
Cognition requires awareness
Neither functions without consciousness
items.inference: One neither engages with the hateful nor knows anything without consciousness.
items.plain_english: One does not proceed toward the hateful, nor does one know, without consciousness.

rows.grounds: the power of rest or completion

items.question: What is the essential nature of the power of cessation?
premises: Cessation is a power of consciousness
Powers of consciousness have intrinsic nature
This power is characterized as bliss
items.inference: The power of cessation is of the nature of bliss.
items.plain_english: The power of cessation is of the nature of bliss.

rows.grounds: in a state of otherness or separation

items.question: Can Shiva be said to have union with bliss-power if he were in a state of otherness?
premises: Union implies relation between distinct entities
A state of otherness would imply separation
Shiva's nature is not separate from his powers
items.inference: If one assumes a state of otherness, union with that power would not apply to him.
items.plain_english: And if it is said that he has no union with that power, that would be in a state of otherness.

items.question: What is the status of knowledge in relation to Shiva's own nature?
premises: Shiva is the supreme reality
Knowledge is awareness-filled
Such knowledge is not acquired externally
items.inference: Knowledge consisting of awareness is always innate to Shiva.
items.plain_english: The knowledge of Shiva, consisting of awareness, is always innate.

rows.grounds: being an intrinsic attribute of the self
in an external source of awakening

items.question: Is Shiva's knowledge an intrinsic attribute or dependent on an external awakener?
premises: Knowledge is innate to Shiva
Intrinsic attributes belong to the self
External dependence would contradict innateness
items.inference: Its self-nature is accepted, not dependence on another awakener.
items.plain_english: It is accepted as his own intrinsic nature, not as belonging to another awakener.

items.question: How are higher and lower states related within the one reality?
premises: Reality manifests in degrees
Higher and lower states are distinguished
All remain situated within the same ground
items.inference: Higher and lower states are situated within that reality.
items.plain_english: Or the higher and lower states are situated there.

rows.grounds: in the state of pure power

items.question: How does the divine reality manifest at the level of pure power?
premises: The divine reality expands into states
Manifestation occurs in degrees
One such degree is pure power
items.inference: Thus expanded, the Lord sometimes abides in the state of pure power.
items.plain_english: Thus expanded, the Lord sometimes abides in the state of pure power.

rows.grounds: in rising or manifestation; reading uncertain

items.question: What further states does the divine reality assume beyond pure power?
premises: Manifestation proceeds through levels
Sadashiva and Ishvara are distinct levels
The Lord assumes these states at times
items.inference: From that emergence he sometimes assumes the Sadashiva state and sometimes the lordly state.
uncertainties: The token udre[1 ] is obscure and its exact form or meaning is uncertain.
items.plain_english: Sometimes he assumes the state of Sadashiva, and sometimes the lordly state of Ishvara.

rows.grounds: the condition of lords of knowledge
the selfhood of mantra and mantra-lords

items.question: Which intermediate tattva states does the divine reality assume in descent?
premises: The descent includes multiple levels
Vidya and Vidyeshvara are such levels
Mantra and Mantreshvara are further levels
items.inference: He assumes the states of knowledge, lords of knowledge, mantra, and mantra-lords.
items.plain_english: He assumes the states of pure knowledge, lords of knowledge, mantra, and mantra-lords.

rows.grounds: and so forth in this manner
the form of the thirty-six principles

items.question: How far does the divine assumption of forms extend in the tattva hierarchy?
premises: Manifestation continues downward
Maya is included in this descent
The full system comprises thirty-six principles
items.inference: The descent extends through maya and so on to the form of the thirty-six principles.
items.plain_english: He assumes the form of maya and so on, down to the form of the thirty-six principles.

rows.grounds: forms ranging from highest to lowest to middle

items.question: How does the divine reality move among superior, middle, and inferior forms?
premises: The divine reality assumes multiple forms
Forms vary in grade
Assuming one form involves releasing another
items.inference: Releasing one form, it takes up superior, inferior, and middle forms.
items.plain_english: Abandoning one form, it takes on superior, inferior, and middle forms.
